whisper: This robot's skin is alive! They grew it from human cells, then attached it to a mechanical face and made it smile. Tiny anchors hold the skin while motors pull underneath. But an earlier experiment gets stranger. They cut living skin on a robotic finger, added a collagen patch, and gave the tissue seven days to repair. Cells grew into the patch, helping close the damage. The machine isn't alive, but the skin it's wearing is.
